This pattern is often used to convert a checked exception into an unchecked one when the error indicates an invalid argument (i.e., the provided `MediaDescription` has an invalid or unexpected media type). The programmer's intent is to signal a problem with the input that should not normally occur if the caller provides valid data. The logging at debug level suggests the programmer wants to trace the issue during development but does not expect the exception to be caught by typical callers; rather, it is meant to propagate up to an appropriate error handler or crash the current operation. The method signature does not declare any thrown exceptions, reinforcing that this runtime exception is not part of the method's contractual obligation.
